verdict.summary: A feature-flag environment value on featureflagservice was set to enable productCatalogFailure at 11:21, and productcatalogservice consequently returns errors on GetProduct calls that consult that flag.
verdict.reasoning: productcatalogservice error ratio rose from an exactly-zero baseline with change points at 11:25 and 11:28 (tr_de4adfafe584), yet nothing was deployed or changed on productcatalogservice itself (tr_42cf030803b1). Traces show every errored productcatalogservice span carries a child call to FeatureFlagService/GetFlag, while non-errored sibling spans do not, and the error propagates upward into frontend roots (tr_05cd16ae4245), which explains why frontend and loadgenerator alerted first without being broken. The change log shows a flag value enabling productCatalogFailure set at 11:21:51, minutes before onset, with two earlier set/revert cycles matching the same pattern (tr_fabe04765fba). The failing mechanism is the wrongness of the configured value itself, not a slow dependency or an exhausted resource: the errored spans complete in milliseconds.
open_questions: Whether the earlier multi-second ListProducts slow-request warnings around 11:03-11:09 (tr_68173ce04b9b) share this cause or are an unrelated pre-existing latency condition.
Whether the 11:21 change was a deliberate fault-injection exercise or an automation error.
featureflagservice's own metrics and logs were not examined, so its post-11:21 serving behaviour is inferred from traces and the change log only.
